summary: J. J. C. Smart was a philosopher who studied at the University of Glasgow (~1938–1946) and The Queen's College, Oxford (~1946–1948). He held posts at the University of Adelaide (~1950–1972), La Trobe University (~1972–1976), and the Australian National University (~1976–1985).

Sinologist J. J. L. Duyvendak studied at Leiden, the Sorbonne, and Berlin, learning under Édouard Chavannes and Henri Cordier. After serving at the Dutch Legation in Peking (1912–1918), he taught at Leiden (1919; 1930–1954) and held visiting professorships at Columbia, Princeton, and Oxford.
J. M. E. McTaggart was a philosopher who was educated at Clifton College (~1882–1885). He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1897 to 1923.
Working in Buddhist studies and other fields, J. Mark G. Williams studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He served as Director at the University of Oxford from circa 2003 to 2016.

Specializing in linguistics, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, J. P. Mallory studied at Occidental College and UCLA. He served on the faculty at Queen's University Belfast (~1977–2011) and as Professor of Prehistoric Archaeology at Queen's University at Kingston (attested 2014).

J. Thomas Rimer is a Japanologist who studied at Princeton and Columbia. His academic career included positions at Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1983), the University of California, Los Angeles, the University of Pittsburgh (~1991–2011), and the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2006).
Jaan Puhvel studied under Stig Wikander (~1951–1952) and Georges Dumézil (~1952–1953).

Jack Copeland is a philosopher and computational scholar who studied at Corpus Christi College and the University of Oxford (~1975–1979). He held positions at the University of Portsmouth and the University of Canterbury (1985).

Jack Goody, an archaeologist and historian, was educated at St Albans School and St John's College (~1938–1946). He held a post as a retired professor at the University of Cambridge from circa 1984 to 2015.

Jack Kornfield studied at Dartmouth under Wing-tsit Chan, at Saybrook University, and under Ajahn Chah, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Dipa Ma. Working in Buddhist and religious studies, he co-founded the Insight Meditation Society (1974) and Spirit Rock Meditation Center (1987).
Jack Laughlin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from McMaster University in 1999. He held a post at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Dalton specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD from the University of Michigan (2002) under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held positions at SOAS, Yale (2005), and UC Berkeley, where he is Distinguished University Professor.
Indologist Jacob Ensink completed his doctoral degree at Utrecht University (~1946–1952) under Jan Gonda. He was appointed lecturer and later professor at the University of Groningen in 1954.

Jacob Grimm, a scholar of linguistics and history, studied at the University of Marburg (~1802–1805). He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1837) and Frederick William University Berlin (1841).
Jacob Holubeck is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).

Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He held posts as Assistant Professor of Religion at the College of William & Mary and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Religious studies scholar Jacob Neusner studied at Harvard, Lincoln College, Columbia, and the Jewish Theological Seminary. He held positions at UW–Milwaukee (~1961–1962), Brandeis (~1962–1964), the University of South Florida (~1990–2000), and Bard College (~1994–2014).

Indologist Jacob Samuel Speyer completed his PhD at Leiden University (~1867–1872) under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He held posts at the University of Amsterdam (1877–1889), University of Groningen (1888–1903), and Leiden University (1903–1913).

Indologist and linguist Jacob Wackernagel studied under Friedrich Nietzsche and Theodor Benfey at Basel, Göttingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at the University of Basel (1876–1902, 1915–1936) and the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).

Jacqueline I. Stone is a scholar of Buddhist and Japanese studies who studied at SFSU and UCLA under William R. LaFleur. She served as Professor at Princeton University (1990–2019) and holds an affiliation with Minobusan University (attested 2026).
